info.title: GainTrace API
info.description:
The GainTrace REST API (v1). Read your customer data and push product-usage events, metric events, and signals into GainTrace.

All endpoints are authenticated with a Bearer API key and scoped to a single workspace.

Each API key can send 60 requests a minute. A `429` response includes a `Retry-After` header with the seconds to wait.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's Companies, most recently updated first. Money fields are integer minor units of `currency`. Renewal dates are `contractStartDate` and `contractEndDate`, and `autoRenew`.

Archived Companies are left out unless you send `includeArchived=true`. A Company is archived when its source removed it. Each record has `archivedAt`, which is `null` for a live Company.

**Scope:** `read:companies`

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on name or domain.

post.description:
Creates a Company, or updates the one that has the same `externalId` (upsert). `externalId` defaults to a slug of `name`.

- A new Company counts against your Company limit (`402` when it is reached). Updating an existing one does not.
- Creating a Company also fires the `company.created` webhook with `source` set to `api`, and starts any Flow that triggers on a new Company. Updating one fires `company.updated` with `changedFields`.
- When an existing Company is updated and is linked to a connection with write-back turned on, the change is queued to sync to the source system.

**Scope:** `write:companies`

get.description:
Returns non-dismissed signals for the workspace, most recent first. Each item has `accountId` (the legacy record id) and `companyId` (the Company id).

**Scope:** `read:signals`

post.description:
Records a signal against a Company in the workspace. Name the Company in `accountId` with its Company `id` or the legacy account id.

- The `201` response returns the signal `id`, the legacy `accountId` and the `companyId`.
- The `signal.created` webhook fires with `source` set to `api`.
- Signals you create keep their own row. GainTrace's detection never merges them with detected signals, and they are never counted as GainTrace predictions.
- Metadata can't use the reserved keys `originalType`, `goldenAccountId` or `golden_account_id`.

**Scope:** `write:signals`

accountId.description: The legacy account id the signal is attached to.

post.description:
Ingests a batch of product-usage events. The shape is Segment-compatible: the GainTrace Segment destination sends here with `source` set to `segment` and the Segment `messageId` as `source_event_id`. Events feed health, signals and activation.

**Keys.** Use a secret key (`gt_live_`, scope `write:events`) from your backend. Use a publishable key (`gt_pub_`, scope `write:ingest`) from a browser. Publishable keys need a browser `Origin` header and are pinned to their allowed origins. The endpoint answers CORS preflight.

**Limits.** 1 to 1000 events per request. Replays are safe: an event whose `(source, source_event_id)` was already stored is reported as `duplicate`. Events with `source` of `sdk`, `warehouse` or `segment` must carry a `source_event_id`.

**Per-event results.** The response has one entry in `results` for each event you sent, in the same order, so you can retry only what failed. Events that fail validation are listed in `validation_errors` and do not stop the rest of the batch. If none of the events are valid, the response is `422`.

**Plan limit.** When the monthly event limit is reached the request fails with `402`, unless pay-as-you-go is on. Overage is billed from the events actually stored, so duplicates and retries are not billed.

**Scope:** `write:events` or `write:ingest`

201.description: The batch was processed. `201` is returned even when some events were duplicates or were rejected, so check `results`.

duplicates.description: Events skipped because their `source_event_id` was already stored.

linked.description: Events attached to a Company, either through `account_id` or by finding the Person in `user_id`.

errors.description: Valid events that GainTrace could not store.

validation_errors.description: Present only when some events failed validation.

results.reason: event_name is required and must be a string

validation_errors.error: event_name is required and must be a string

422.description: The `events` array is missing, empty or over 1000, or no event in it is valid. When no event is valid, the body also carries `validation_errors`.

error.message: No valid events in request. See validation_errors for the per-event reasons.

validation_errors.error: source_event_id is required for source 'segment' (used for deduplication)

post.description:
Ingests a batch of typed metric events into the metrics engine (feeds daily snapshots that calc metrics evaluate). Idempotent on `(source, externalId)`; duplicates are skipped silently. Returns a per-event outcome.

**Scope:** `write:events` · **1 to 500 events per request.**

202.description: Batch processed. See `outcomes` for per-event status.

get.description:
Fetch one Company by UUID, or by `ext:<externalId>`. An archived Company is still returned here, with `archivedAt` set.

**Scope:** `read:companies`

patch.description:
Updates the mutable fields of an existing Company, addressed by UUID or `ext:<externalId>`. Send at least one field. If the Company is linked to a connection with write-back turned on, the change is queued to sync to the source system. There is no delete endpoint for Companies.

**Scope:** `write:companies`

get.description:
Fetch one signal by id.

**Scope:** `read:signals`

patch.description:
Update a signal's title, description, severity, snooze, or metadata. Metadata can't use the reserved keys `originalType`, `goldenAccountId` or `golden_account_id` (`422`), and any reserved key already stored on the signal is kept.

**Scope:** `write:signals`

post.description:
Create up to 1000 signals. Partial success: each item reports its own outcome, and one bad item never fails the batch. Each item's `accountId` takes a Company `id` or the legacy account id. An id GainTrace can't find fails that item with a message that starts `Couldn't find the Company`. Each created signal fires `signal.created` with `source` set to `api`. Batches of more than 25 signals are delivered in paced batches instead of right away.

**Scope:** `write:signals`

get.description:
The original path for `GET /people`. It returns the same records in the same shape, and takes the same `includeArchived` parameter. Archived records are left out by default.

**Scope:** `read:contacts`

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only People at this Company.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact match.

post.description:
The original path for `POST /people`. Same body, same rules, same responses.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

delete.summary: Delete a person everywhere by key
delete.description:
Deletes a Person by your own key, for privacy-deletion requests. Pass `externalId` or `email`. GainTrace removes the Person's records at **every** Company, archived ones included, and fires `contact.deleted` for each. It is idempotent: if nobody matches, the response is still `204`.

This is the same operation as `DELETE /people`. Their survey data is erased too: answers to your surveys are anonymized (name, email and free text removed, scores and choices kept), imported answers are deleted, and their short personal survey links are deleted.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Used when `externalId` is absent.

get.description:
The original path for `GET /people/{id}`. An archived record is still returned, with `archivedAt` set.

**Scope:** `read:contacts`

patch.description:
The original path for `PATCH /people/{id}`. Same body, same rules, including how an `email` change moves the whole Person and the `409` when another Person already uses the address.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

delete.description:
The original path for `DELETE /people/{id}`. Deletes this one record only. Their survey data is erased too, except where they belong to another Company: answers to your surveys are anonymized (name, email and free text removed, scores and choices kept), imported answers are deleted, and their short personal survey links are deleted. Answers that carry only an email address are kept while another record in the workspace still has that email.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

get.description:
List the workspace's webhook subscriptions.

**Scope:** `read:webhooks`

post.description:
Register a webhook subscription. The signing `secret` is returned only in this response.

The key needs `write:webhooks` and the read scope of every event you subscribe to: `read:companies` for `company.*`, `read:contacts` for `contact.*`, `read:signals` for `signal.created`, and `read:surveys` for `survey.*` and `survey_response.*`. `member.*` events need no read scope. Subscribing to `*` needs all four read scopes. A key without one of them gets `403` with the message `This key can't subscribe to <event>. Add the <scope> scope.`

**Scope:** `write:webhooks`

get.description:
Fetch one webhook.

**Scope:** `read:webhooks`

patch.description:
Update url, events, headers, description, or active state. Changing `events` needs the same read scopes as creating a subscription: `read:companies` for `company.*`, `read:contacts` for `contact.*`, `read:signals` for `signal.created`, and `read:surveys` for `survey.*` and `survey_response.*`. `*` needs all four. A key without one gets `403`. Setting `active` to `true` clears the failure count and the auto-disable.

**Scope:** `write:webhooks`

delete.description:
Delete a webhook and its delivery history.

**Scope:** `write:webhooks`

post.description:
Send a signed `ping` to the endpoint now and return the result.

**Scope:** `write:webhooks`

get.description:
Returns People, most recently updated first. A Person who belongs to several Companies appears once for each Company. Filter by Company, email or your own id.

Archived records are left out unless you send `includeArchived=true`. A record is archived when the Person left that Company or its source removed them. Each record has `archivedAt`, which is `null` for a live one.

**Scope:** `read:contacts`

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only People at this Company.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Exact match.

post.description:
Adds a Person to a Company.

- Name the Company with `accountId` or `accountExternalId`.
- A Person who already exists at a **different** Company gets a new record at this one. Matching is by `externalId`, then `email`. That does not count against your People limit.
- A Person who already exists at **this** Company fails with `409`, unless you send `upsert: true`. Then the record is updated and returned with `200`, and `traits` are merged.
- A new Person counts against your People limit (`402` when it is reached).
- With `accountExternalId`, an unknown Company is created for you and counts against your Company limit. It fires the `company.created` webhook with `source` set to `api`. It does not start Company-created Flows.
- A new Person fires `contact.created`, and an upsert that updates a Person fires `contact.updated`, both with `source` set to `api`.

This is the same operation as `POST /contacts`.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

200.description: The Person already existed at this Company and `upsert` was true. The updated record.

delete.description:
Deletes a Person by your own key, for privacy-deletion requests. Pass `externalId` or `email`; `externalId` is tried first. GainTrace removes the Person's records at **every** Company, archived ones included, and fires `contact.deleted` for each, with `source` set to `api`. It is idempotent: if nobody matches, the response is still `204`. Send neither parameter and the call returns `422`.

This is the same operation as `DELETE /contacts`. To remove a single record, use `DELETE /people/{id}`. Their survey data is erased too: answers to your surveys are anonymized (name, email and free text removed, scores and choices kept), imported answers are deleted, and their short personal survey links are deleted.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Used when `externalId` is absent.

get.description:
Fetch one Person at one Company by `id`. An archived record is still returned here, with `archivedAt` set.

**Scope:** `read:contacts`

patch.description:
Updates the mutable fields of one Person record. Send at least one field. If the Company is linked to a connection with write-back turned on, the change is queued to sync to the source system.

**Changing `email`.** An email change moves the whole Person, not one record. Every live record of this Person, at every Company, takes the new address, and each fires `contact.updated` with `changedFields` set to `["email"]`. The call returns `409` `conflict` when a different Person in the workspace already uses the address, including a Person whose records are all archived. Addresses are compared without regard to case or surrounding spaces. Changing only the letter case, or sending `email: null`, stays on this one record.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

delete.description:
Permanently deletes this one record. If the same human is also at other Companies, those records stay. To remove a human everywhere, use `DELETE /people` with `externalId` or `email`. Fires `contact.deleted`. Their survey data is erased too, except where they belong to another Company: answers to your surveys are anonymized (name, email and free text removed, scores and choices kept), imported answers are deleted, and their short personal survey links are deleted. Answers that carry only an email address are kept while another record in the workspace still has that email.

**Scope:** `write:contacts`

get.description:
Returns NPS answers from every source, newest first: answers collected by GainTrace surveys and answers imported through `POST /nps-responses`. Requires a secret key (`gt_live_`); a publishable key gets `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Only answers imported from this provider.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only answers from this Company.

parameters.name: contactId
parameters.description: Only answers from this Person.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only answers on or after this time. ISO 8601 with a UTC offset.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only answers on or before this time. ISO 8601 with a UTC offset.

post.description:
Imports one NPS answer from another survey tool. Send one answer per request. Requires a secret key (`gt_live_`); a publishable key gets `403`.

- **Idempotent.** `provider` and `externalId` together identify the answer. Sending the same pair again updates the stored answer instead of adding a second one. The response is `200` either way.
- **Who answered.** Send `contactId`, or send both `accountId` and `email`. With `contactId`, the Company and email come from that Person. With `accountId` and `email`, GainTrace tries to match a Person at that Company and leaves `contactId` null when it cannot.
- **Category.** GainTrace sets `category` from `score`: 9-10 promoter, 7-8 passive, 0-6 detractor.
- **Stored with your other NPS.** The answer is saved with `source` set to `api:<provider>`, next to answers collected by GainTrace surveys. A `comment` is read for themes.
- **Webhook.** A new answer fires `survey_response.created`. A repeat of an answer you already imported fires `survey_response.updated`. Imported answers have `surveyId: null` and `channel: import`.
- **No outreach.** The import does not send survey emails or follow-up messages.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

200.description: The stored answer, whether it was new or an update.

400.description: The `contactId` does not match the `accountId` or `email` you sent, or the request was not valid JSON.

get.description:
List the survey templates the workspace saved, each with its full survey definition. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

post.description:
Save a template from an existing survey (`surveyId`) or from a survey definition (`input`). A name another template uses returns `422`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

surveyId.description: Save this survey as a template. Send this or `input`, not both.

422.description: The name is already used, or the survey definition is invalid.

patch.description:
Edit a survey. Send any subset of the survey contract. Once a survey is `active` or has any responses, changing `type`, `questions` or `settings.anonymous` is refused with `400`, because it would change what past answers mean. Duplicate the survey in the app to change those. Name, cooldown and the other settings stay editable. The merged result is validated as a whole, so a patch can fail on a rule that involves a key you did not send. Rules that compare several fields (a required first question, the NPS 0-10 and CSAT/CES scale ranges, promotional copy, `showWhen` rules) are checked after the merge, and a failure returns `400` `bad_request` with a generic message and no field detail. A value that fails its own field schema returns `422`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

questions.text: How likely are you to recommend us to a colleague?
What is the main reason for your score?

post.description:
Launch a draft, close a survey, or reopen a closed one. Launching validates the survey contract again. A launched survey can't return to draft, so only `active` and `closed` are accepted. Moving to `active` or `closed` fires the `survey.launched` or `survey.closed` webhook. Sending the status the survey already has changes nothing and fires nothing. If the launch re-validation fails a cross-field rule, the call returns `400` `bad_request` with a generic message and no field detail. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

200.description: The survey with its new status.

post.description:
Request email invitations for up to 100 people (`personIds`), or for everyone a saved segment (`segmentId`) or a set of Company and People rules (`audience`) matches, up to 1,000 people. The survey must be `active`.

**Send or approve.** Workspaces send by default: each invitation is released to send right away, or at the survey's next send window. A workspace can switch to approval, where invitations wait in Triage until a teammate approves them, and approvals expire after 14 days. The result's `mode` says which applied. Invitations sent by an API key follow the workspace setting.

**Who is skipped.** People are skipped, not failed, when an invitation for their email already waits or is about to send, when they are inside the survey's `cooldownDays`, or when the workspace frequency rule applies. The response counts them but does not name them. To preview who would be invited, use the `gt_survey_request_invitations` MCP tool, which defaults to a dry run.

**Errors.** With `personIds`, every person must be active, have an email address and belong to a Company, or the whole request returns `400` and nothing is queued. A `segmentId` that is missing or archived returns `404`. An audience that matches more than 1,000 people returns `400`: narrow the rules or split them into segments. An `audience` with no rules, or a body with more than one of the three keys, returns `422`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

Record an answer that your own app, bot or form collected from a known person. It runs the same validation, attribution and follow-through as an emailed survey: the response appears in the inbox, fires signals and Flows, and sends the `survey_response.created` webhook with `channel` set to `api`. Send `subject` to tie the answer to a deal, ticket, plan or custom record. The survey must be `active`; otherwise the call returns `404`. Re-sending the same `externalId` for the same survey is safe: the first response is returned with `duplicate: true` and `200`, and the new body is ignored. The first call returns `201`. On an anonymous survey the response is stored without a person or company. Answers that don't fit the survey's questions, and a `subject` GainTrace can't link, return `422`. A body that fails its own field schema also returns `422`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

200.description: This `externalId` was already recorded. The first response is returned.

post.description:
Decide whether to show an in-app survey to a signed-in person, and mint the signed embed URL if so. Call it from your backend, never from a browser: a request that carries an `Origin` header is refused with `403`, and cross-origin preflight requests are refused too. (Browser code uses a signed identity token with the in-app SDK instead. See the in-app SDK guide.) It returns `200` for both outcomes. When the person qualifies you get `eligible: true`, an `embedUrl` that is valid for one hour, a `sessionId` and the configured `delayMs`. Otherwise you get `eligible: false` and a `reason`: `disabled` (survey not active or in-app collection off), `cooldown`, `recently_dismissed`, `not_sampled`, `snoozed`, `already_seen`, `minimum_age`, `minimum_sessions`, `display_limit`, or, when the survey has targeting, `page_not_targeted`, `not_targeted` or `awaiting_trigger`. A survey with page rules needs `context.url`; without it the reason is `page_not_targeted`. A person who passes the earlier checks gets one recorded session per UTC day, and those count toward `minSessions`. `parentOrigin` must be listed in `settings.inApp.allowedOrigins`, or the call returns `403`. The person must exist, be active and belong to `accountId`, or the call returns `404`. Send `subject` to tie the survey to a deal, ticket, plan or custom record; a record GainTrace can't link returns `422`. Any invalid or malformed body, or an invalid survey id, returns `422`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

get.description:
Read the workspace-wide rule that limits how often one person is surveyed, across every survey and channel. A workspace that never changed it gets the defaults, 30 and 7 days. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

put.description:
Replace the workspace's frequency rule. Send both day fields. `0` turns a person rule off. `companyLimit` is optional: send `null` to turn the Company limit off, or leave it out to keep it. The rule applies to email invitations and in-app sessions. It does not block responses you record through the API. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

get.description:
Read how new responses are owned and how long they can wait. A workspace that never changed the rules gets 48 hours and `negative`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

put.description:
Replace the workspace's response rules. Send both fields. It decides who owns new responses and when an open response is overdue. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

get.description:
List responses from every GainTrace survey (NPS, CSAT, CES and custom), newest first, across the email, in-app and API channels, plus older answers collected before public links, QR codes and kiosks were removed. Responses imported through the NPS import endpoint are not included. Filters combine with AND. An unknown query parameter returns `422`. Pagination is `limit` and `offset`; there is no cursor. `from` and `to` are inclusive and compare against `submittedAt`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Review status. `open` means any status except `resolved`. `overdue` means open past the workspace hours-to-close rule (`GET /surveys/case-rules`).

get.description:
List the workspace's saved survey segments, by name. Archived segments are left out. The list is not paged: `meta.count` is the number of segments. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

post.description:
Save a segment of Company and People rules. Use it as a survey's in-app audience (`settings.inApp.targeting.audience.segmentId`) or as the audience of an invitation request (`segmentId`). The name must be unique in the workspace, ignoring case; a name already in use returns `422`. A segment needs at least one rule across the two groups. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

delete.description:
Archive a saved segment. It leaves the list and its name becomes free to use again. A survey whose in-app audience still points at it stops matching anyone until you choose a new audience, and an invitation request with its `segmentId` returns `404`. A segment that doesn't exist, or is already archived, returns `404`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The segment's UUID.

get.description:
List the survey tools connected to your workspace (Typeform, SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics and Retently), newest first, with the status of their latest pull. Credentials are never returned. You connect and disconnect sources in the app. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

post.summary: Pull a survey import source now
post.description:
Pull one connected source now instead of waiting for the hourly schedule. The call waits for the pull, up to 60 seconds, and returns what it found. Imported scores count toward Company scores next to your own surveys' responses. Imported NPS also counts toward coverage; imported CSAT and CES do not. The call returns `409` while another pull of the same source is running, and when the source's credential was rejected. It returns `404` for a source outside your workspace. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `write:surveys`

200.description: The pull finished or stopped early.

skip_reasons.reason: No email on this response. Map an email field so GainTrace can match the person.

get.description:
Results for every question of one survey, shaped by the answer type: counts per choice, means for scores, ranking scores, matrix rows, date ranges and, for the product-market fit question, the share who would be very disappointed. Written answers are counted but never returned. Use `GET /survey-responses` to read individual responses. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

What is the main reason for your score?

get.description:
Company NPS against a product usage metric and ARR. Company scores follow your rollup rules. The response carries a 95% margin of error with every NPS, plus plain and revenue-weighted NPS across the workspace. Archived Companies are left out. A Company with no usage value or no ARR is reported in `missing`, never as zero. Without `metric`, GainTrace uses the first of `events_30d`, `engagement_score`, `dau_wau_ratio` and `seat_utilization` that has data, or else your most-covered metric definition. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: The usage metric: `events_30d`, `active_people_30d`, `active_days_30d`, `engagement_score`, `dau_wau_ratio`, `seat_utilization`, `event:<name>` for one product event, or `def:<id>` for a metric definition. Take values from `metrics` in a previous response. A value in the wrong format returns `400`. A well-formed metric your workspace has no data for returns `404`.

get.description:
Inferred satisfaction for one Company: a calibrated 1 to 5 estimate per Person, beside their surveyed score. The response is empty (`company` is `null` and `people` is an empty list) until an admin turns inferred satisfaction on in the app and at least 20 People have both an inferred and a surveyed score to compare. Pass the Company `id`; `ext:<externalId>` isn't accepted, and an id that isn't a UUID returns `400`. A Company outside your workspace returns `404`. Requires a secret server key (`gt_live_`). Publishable keys (`gt_pub_`) return `403`.

**Scope:** `read:surveys`

people.description: People whose answers count toward this measure.

reportingCurrency.description: The workspace reporting currency the ARR figures are in.

arrTotal.description: ARR of all Companies in minor units of the reporting currency. Null when no Company has ARR.

arrHeard.description: ARR of the Companies heard from, in minor units of the reporting currency.

unconvertedCurrencies.description: Currencies left out of the ARR figures because no exchange rate exists for them yet.

silentRenewals.description: Companies renewing in the next 90 days that nobody has heard from in 180 days.

companiesInferredOnly.description: Companies that have an inferred satisfaction score but no scored survey answer in the window. `null` until an admin turns on inferred satisfaction and it has enough People to calibrate. These Companies are never counted in `companiesHeard`.

field.description: In a Company rule group, a field key from your Company data model, such as `segment` or `plan`. In a People rule group, one of `email`, `name`, `role`, `contactRole`, `isChampion`, `lastSeenAt`, `engagementScore`, `createdAt`, or `traits.<key>` for a Person trait. `person.` and `people.` prefixes are accepted. Any other People field returns `422`.

operator.description: The same operators Flow conditions use.

unit.description: The unit for date operators such as `in_the_last`.

SurveyAudienceRules.description: Who to reach: People who match `person`, at Companies that match `company`. An empty `rules` list in a group matches everyone for that group. A request needs at least one rule across both groups, so nobody is ever invited by accident. Only People with an email address at Companies that aren't archived can match.

name.description: Unique in the workspace, ignoring case.

SurveySubjectInput.description: The record a response is about: a deal, ticket, plan or custom record. Name it by its GainTrace `id`, or, for a deal or ticket, by the id it has in your CRM or help desk (`externalId`, with `source` when more than one connection holds that id). For a custom record, send the data model's `model` slug and the record's `externalId`. The record must exist, must not be archived, and must belong to the same Company as the person.

source.description: The connection the id comes from, such as `hubspot`. Lowercased.

SurveySubject.description: The record the response is about.

value.description: A path and query such as `/billing`. No spaces, and nothing after `#`.

SurveyInAppTargeting.description: Who, where and when the in-app survey shows. GainTrace checks the page rules first, then the audience, then the trigger. People who don't qualify get a reason from `POST /surveys/{id}/session`.

audience.description: Limit the survey to a saved segment, or to rules you send here.

pages.description: Page rules matched against the `context.url` your backend sends when it mints a session. With include rules, the page must match one. A page that matches an exclude rule never shows the survey.

trigger.description: What makes the survey appear. Without a trigger it shows as soon as the person qualifies.

events.description: Event names your code sends with `GaintraceSurveys.track()`.

SurveyLanguageCopy.description: The copy for one language. Anything you leave out falls back to the default language. A question translation applies only while the default copy it was written against is unchanged: GainTrace stamps a `source` fingerprint on save, and a translation whose fingerprint no longer matches is ignored until you update it.

title.description: The survey name shown as the heading.

questions.description: One entry per question, in order. Use `null` for a question you don't translate.

source.description: Fingerprint of the default copy. GainTrace sets it on save when you leave it out.

options.description: Same length and order as the default `options`.

rows.description: Same length and order as the default `rows`.

ui.description: Overrides for the respondent page's interface strings, keyed by string id. An unknown key returns `422`.

SurveyQuestionAnswer.description: One answer paired with its question wording. Statements and unanswered questions are left out.

key.description: `q0`, `q1` and so on, the same key as in `answers`.

value.description: The stored answer: a number for a score, a string for text, a choice, or a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, a list of strings for checkboxes and rankings (in rank order), an object of row to column for a matrix, and `true` for consent.

display.description: The answer as readable text, for example `Reporting, Alerts`.

SurveyImportSource.description: A survey tool connected to your workspace. The credential is never returned.

externalSurveyId.description: The form, survey or campaign id in the provider's tool.

status.description: `error` means the provider rejected the credential. Disconnect the source in the app and connect it again.

credentialHint.description: The last four characters of the stored credential.

lastRun.description: Counts from the most recent run.

status.description: `partial` means the pull stopped before it finished. GainTrace continues on a later pull.

updated.description: Responses that changed since an earlier import.

SurveyQuestionResult.description: Results for one question. Which optional fields appear depends on the question's type.

answered.description: How many responses answered this question.

totalResponses.description: How many responses the survey has.

average.description: Mean score for `rating` and `scale` questions, to two decimals. `null` otherwise, or with no answers.

choices.description: Counts in a fixed order: the scale from lowest to highest, the option order, months for a date, or a single `Agreed` row for consent. Text answers are counted in `answered` but never listed.

ranking.description: `ranking` questions: items from most to least preferred. First place counts for the number of items and last place for 1.

matrix.description: `matrix` questions: one entry per row, with the answers across the shared columns and the average column position, from 1.

dates.description: `date` questions: the earliest and latest date answered.

pmf.description: Questions with `preset: "pmf"`: the four answer counts, the base (the first three answers added up) and the share who would be very disappointed.

percent.description: Percent of the base who would be very disappointed. `null` with an empty base.

questions.description: One entry per question, in survey order.

margin.description: The 95% margin of error, in NPS points.

method.description: `adjusted_wald` is used when every answer falls in one group, so a small sample never reads as a margin of zero.

window.description: How the value is read. `before_answer` covers the 30 days up to the Company's latest answer. `current` is the Company's value now. `latest_value` is the newest recorded value.

companies.description: How many Companies have data for this metric.

method.description: One sentence describing how Company scores were built.

metric.description: The usage metric the points use. `null` when the workspace has no usage data.

metrics.description: Every metric you can send as `metric`. Metrics with no data are not offered.

points.description: One point per Company with NPS answers in the window, largest ARR first. Capped at 2,000.

people.description: People whose answers count toward this Company's NPS.

usage.description: The Company's value for the metric. `null` when it has none, never zero.

arr.description: ARR in minor units of `reportingCurrency`. `null` when the Company has no ARR or no exchange rate exists.

plain.description: NPS across everyone, each Person counted once.

arr.description: ARR of the Companies in the calculation, in minor units of `reportingCurrency`.

revenueWeighted.description: NPS where each Company counts in proportion to its ARR. Companies without ARR are left out.

quadrants.description: Companies split at the median usage and at NPS 0.

truncated.description: `true` when there were more than 2,000 points.

CompanyInferredSatisfaction.description: A Trace AI estimate of how satisfied a Company's People sound, built from their own emails, calls and tickets. It is always separate from NPS, CSAT and CES.

enabled.description: Whether an admin turned inferred satisfaction on.

windowDays.description: How far back a Person's conversations count.

calibration.description: How the estimate compares with People's surveyed scores.

n.description: People who have both an inferred and a surveyed score.

agreementPercent.description: Share of those People whose inferred band matched their surveyed band, checked leave-one-out. `null` below 2 People.

meanAbsoluteError.description: Mean gap on the 1 to 5 scale, checked leave-one-out. `null` below 2 People.

map.description: The calibrated score for raw scores 1 to 5.

published.description: `true` once `n` reaches `minimumN`. Until then no scores are returned.

minimumN.description: How many People must have both scores before estimates are published.

company.description: The Company's score: the plain mean of its People's inferred scores. `null` when there is nothing to show.

people.description: Each Person's estimate beside their latest surveyed score, most negative first.

surveyed.description: The Person's latest surveyed score in the rollup window, never merged with the estimate.
